overview: Two RNA types found in protein synthesis, differing in whether they deliver amino acids or build the ribosome itself.
genZNote: tRNA is the delivery driver bringing amino acids. rRNA is part of the factory building where they get assembled.

aspects.label: Function
aspects.valueA: Transfers specific amino acids to the ribosome, matching codons via its anticodon.
aspects.valueB: Combines with proteins to form the ribosome, catalysing peptide bond formation.

aspects.label: Structure
aspects.valueB: Complex folded structure forming ribosomal subunits.

aspects.label: Relative Size
aspects.valueA: Smallest of the three main RNA types.
aspects.valueB: Largest of the three main RNA types.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: tRNA is the only RNA type with a distinctive clover-leaf secondary structure — a common diagram-ID question.
overlay.memoryTrick: tRNA = transfer (delivers amino acids). rRNA = ribosomal (builds the ribosome).
overlay.commonMisconception: tRNA doesn't just passively carry amino acids — its anticodon actively determines translation accuracy by matching mRNA codons.
